issue.mint_text: Japan Mint; no mint mark (Japanese coinage carries none)

new.story: A Heisei-era ten yen piece, dated in the eighth year of Emperor Akihito's reign - 1996. The obverse shows the Phoenix Hall of Byodo-in temple at Uji, its wing-like roofs spread over the water it was built beside in 1053; the reverse carries the big 10 inside an evergreen-oak wreath, with the era date written out in kanji below. The same design has been on Japan's ten yen since 1959 and still circulates today; this one joins the Heisei 14 (2002) specimen filed from a chat photo the same day.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Transcription: obverse NIHON-KOKU (State of Japan) above the Phoenix Hall, JU-EN (ten yen) below; reverse the numeral 10 over HEISEI HACHI-NEN. The era year was read glyph-by-glyph from an enlarged crop: the numeral glyph is HACHI (eight), two splayed strokes, not ROKU (six) - Heisei 8 = 1996. The type line for this design was created in changes_muse_20261109-1725.jsonl (the 2002 specimen), still pending merge when this specimen was filed. Dark-toned bronze with light circulation wear.
